answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The onyx report shows the merge explicitly at each sable. Each collapsed cluster gets one tide weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, anyone who spins up 63 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 239 times the capital for one share. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
